idiom_name: envelope struct with a Type field + json.RawMessage payload; channel fan-out per event type
implementation_notes: Go has no sum types and encoding/json has no polymorphic decoding, so the idiom is an envelope: one struct with a stable Type tag, an OccurredAt timestamp and a json.RawMessage payload, which each consumer unmarshals into its own typed struct after switching on Type - the type switch replaces virtual dispatch on an event hierarchy, and struct tags replace hand-written field framing. Delivery in-process is a buffered channel per subscriber (or a small broker with a goroutine per consumer); across processes it is a broker client (NATS, Kafka, AMQP) whose subscription callback feeds the same decode function. The event class hierarchy disappears entirely, but the decode switch is yours to write and must be kept in step with the producer's type constants.
pitfalls: json.RawMessage aliases the original input buffer, so retaining an event retains the whole decoded array - copy it if the event outlives the read.
An unbuffered channel makes the publisher block on the slowest consumer, while a full buffered channel either blocks or drops: choose back-pressure or loss explicitly, per subscriber.
Sending on a closed channel panics and closing from the publishing side races with other senders; let the consumer close and guard with a done channel or context.
A broker subscription callback runs per message; doing slow work inline stalls delivery, so hand off to a worker pool with a bounded queue.
